title: Build the deterministic offline evaluation harness
summary: Implement a full offline harness with deterministic fixture responses, controlled clocks and repeatable arm outputs. This exceeds the scaffold walkthrough: it must run complete frozen episodes, report scheduled and unresolved decisions, and exercise faulty provider shapes without claiming semantic accuracy.
in_scope: Fixture executor, clock and fault injection, episode runner
Structured result manifests and deterministic admission replay
out_of_scope: Live provider behavior or measured live usefulness
Marking the harness complete from a documentation or single-example smoke check
implementation: Inject a fake executor keyed by request digest and explicit fixture scenario, rather than generating answers from the same policy being tested.
Run the two arm manifests over complete episodes and persist scheduled, successful, abstained, failed and stale result counts.
Provide deterministic timeout, malformed batch, partial answer, conflicting predicate, changed-source and missing-certificate fixtures.
Validate final lifecycle, assessment and attention expectations derived from independently specified episode outcomes.
Emit a machine-readable mode marker and command/result manifest that identifies all semantic-provider and live-delivery gates as not_run.

acceptance.criterion: The same corpus, fixture set and configuration reproduce identical logical outputs.
acceptance.verification: Run twice with controlled timestamps and compare all result digests excluding execution-instance metadata.

acceptance.criterion: Faulted and abstained scheduled decisions remain in denominators and diagnostics.
acceptance.verification: Inject one of each failure class and reconcile scheduled count with all terminal outcomes.

acceptance.criterion: Offline output cannot be presented as a successful real-provider qualification.
acceptance.verification: Inspect the mode/gate schema and reject a report that claims provider accuracy from fixture mode.

tests: Missing fixture response is an explicit error, not a guessed success.
One malformed head rejects admission while retaining valid diagnostics.
All-silent fake behavior fails an episode that needs a timely contribution.
risks: Tests mirroring implementation can conceal policy errors.
A polished synthetic report can accidentally be mistaken for empirical model evidence.

reuse.application: Adapt strict response and diagnostic/admission separation cases into independent fixture expectations.
